method: Recommendations authored in the current conversation from all 12 complete public evidence packets. No future outcomes or baseline recommendation file read before submission. The assistant knows the authored simulator and baseline source; this is not blinded.

decisions.rationale: Orders rose from 51 to 56 and payment records reconcile. The qualified recent model only adds $1.76 in the static forecast, which omits contact dynamics and shared-budget effects. With no evidence of campaign deterioration, retain the current policy for this seven-day window rather than force 10% offers or make a marginal model change. This is a conservative judgment, not proof that the new model would lose.

The observed rival-promotion feature appears throughout the latest complete week and purchases fell from 46 to 33. The tree passed temporal validation and its shared forecast improves contribution by $58.39, more than blanket 10% offers. Use the qualified candidate while retaining all contact, margin and budget guards. Its prediction improvement is supporting evidence, not a guarantee of campaign lift.

The recent candidate did not pass the shared validation threshold. Keep has the highest permitted forecast. A 10% offer fails the tote margin floor and the other blanket-offer choices also reduce estimated contribution. The sales decline alone does not justify a broader coupon policy.

Payment records are complete, current stock is positive, and the candidate failed the promotion gate. Keep leads the available contribution estimates; a blanket 10% offer adds contacts and slightly reduces estimated value. The recent sales fall is insufficient evidence to override the model or pause organic demand.

Fourteen captures await delayed labels, but payment totals reconcile and completed sales increased. Do not treat the missing labels as failed purchases. The recent model was rejected and no permitted alternative beats keep in the shared forecast. Preserve the product-specific margin safeguards instead of expanding coupons while labels catch up.

Every product falls below the 20% margin floor even at a 5% discount. Pause coupon proposals and preserve organic purchases. A better predictive model cannot repair these unit economics. The executor already blocks these offers, so I expect little or no financial advantage over simply keeping the guarded policy.

Sales are stable, the candidate is worse than the champion, and keep leads every permitted forecast. Two products cannot support 10% offers; only 32 randomized-history observations received 10%, so that conversion rate is weak evidence for a broader campaign. Retain the targeted policy.

Sales fell from 51 to 26 with an observed rival promotion and complete labels. The recent model passed validation. Its retrospective coupon choices tie the current forecast, but updated response scores can change priority under the shared budget as future customer states change. Adopt it for the bounded window rather than offer 10% indiscriminately. This is an uncertain judgment about ranking; the packet does not demonstrate incremental profit.

The validated candidate modestly improves forecast contribution by $3.40 while reducing proposed contacts from 98 to 95. Its more selective allocation fits the uneven product margins; neither blanket 5% nor 10% performs as well in the shared estimates. Use the qualified candidate, acknowledging that the forecast gain is small and not causal proof.

The candidate failed the common promotion gate. Keep has the highest available estimated contribution; blanket 10% increases contacts while reducing forecast contribution by $14.67. Historical 10% response is encouraging but does not establish that expanding the current targeted campaign helps under current shared-budget conditions.

Eighteen captures await labels, while the independent payment ledger shows sales rising. The recent model is valid on the completed window, but its $1.31 forecast gain comes with more proposed contacts and incomplete latest outcomes. Retain the current policy for this bounded window; delay is not a payment failure and does not warrant paid human escalation.

All three products fail the 20% coupon margin floor, including at 5%; some discounted orders have negative unit contribution. Pause offers and leave organic purchases possible. Model validation cannot fix the cost problem. The existing execution guard already prevents these discounts, so no material uplift from this decision is assumed.
